analysis.title: Antero Midstream Corp. (AM): Soft Quarter Highlights Price Sensitivity, but Upside Growth Potential Increasing
key_insights: GS stays Neutral on Antero Midstream (AM) with an unchanged 12-month price target of $24, based on 11.0x 2027 EBITDA. Price was $21.47 at the 30 Oct 2026 close, implying 11.8% upside.
3Q26 adj. EBITDA was $291m, below GSe of $314m and FactSet consensus of $313m (-7% each). EBITDA was up 1% QoQ against management's guidance for high-single-digit sequential growth, and up 3% YoY.

The miss came from lower Gathering & Compression volumes and margins and lower Water volumes. JV distributions were in line. Gathering volumes fell 1% QoQ on curtailments but rose 19% YoY on the HG acquisition and sponsor AR's development cadence.
Fresh water volumes were 89 kb/d, up 9% QoQ but below GSe of 105 kb/d. Margins were largely in line with expectations.
Management left 2026 EBITDA guidance unchanged at $1,190-1,240m. GSe is now $1,191m, at the low end, versus consensus of $1,211m. Capex guidance of $190-220m was also unchanged, versus GSe of $220m.
Adj. FCF after dividends guidance rose to $700-760m from $330-390m, reflecting $377m of Veolia litigation proceeds. GSe is $702m.

Sponsor AR cut its 4Q26 production outlook to about 4.3 bcfe/d from 4.4-4.5 bcfe/d. AR curtailed about 10 bcfe in 3Q26 versus guidance of about 5 bcfe, and expects 15-20 bcfe of curtailments in 4Q26 on weak shoulder-season pricing and third-party downstream outages.

GS estimates the incremental 3Q26 curtailments cut G&C operating income by about $3-4m, and the 4Q26 guide implies an impact of about $11-12m. GS sees AM volumes as partly gas-price dependent in weak pricing windows.
GS models 4Q26 EBITDA of about $323m (+11% QoQ), driven mainly by higher fresh water volumes from two AR DUC growth pads, bringing FY26 to $1,191m.

Management expects double-digit EBITDA growth in 2027, driven by AR production growth (about 4.5 bcfe/d, three rigs and two completion crews), higher fresh water deliveries, and a full year of the integrated HG water system. Off a base of about $1,190m, about 10% growth implies about $1,310m, just below GSe of $1,315m.

Management sized regional infrastructure opportunities at several billion dollars, covering regional pipelines, laterals to demand centers and integrated power. It described the demand as pull from LNG, utilities and electrification rather than producer push.

East Side Express (ESE) scope is unchanged at $200-300m, with about 7 interconnects and a late 2028-2029 in-service date. A North-South regional pipeline serving the Clarington market could reach FID in 2027.

GS now models a pre-FID North-South line at $500m of capex (larger than ESE) at a 6-8x build multiple, entering service in two phases across 2029-2030. It could replace or de-emphasize Stonewall. GS excludes other pre-FID projects pending detail on contracting and returns.
Gas transmission projects could reduce AM's indirect gas and NGL price exposure.

Buybacks were about $27m versus GSe of about $89m. Management gave no forward pace and flagged $100m+ of 2027 capex above the organic program for ESE and other regional projects. About $283m remains on the authorization.

Leverage is 2.8x, below the 3x target, after the $377m Veolia inflow was applied to debt reduction in July. GS expects buybacks to continue at a slower pace through 2027-2030, and a larger share of FCF to go to repurchases once leverage is sustained at 2.5x.

GS cuts EBITDA estimates about 1% on average for 2026-2028 on lower volumes and raises them about 2% for 2029-2032 on North-South. It now models a 2026-2030 EBITDA CAGR of about 7%, with about 4% annual growth beyond 2030.

market_movers.rationale: Soft 3Q26 on lower volumes and curtailments, with growth upside from regional pipelines. The target uses 11.0x 2027 EBITDA of $1,315m and implies 11.8% upside from $21.47.

earnings_insights: AM 3Q26 adj. EBITDA was reported at $291m versus GSe of $314m and FactSet consensus of $313m, a 7% miss against each. EBITDA was up 1% QoQ and 3% YoY.
AM FY26 EBITDA guidance of $1,190-1,240m is unchanged. GSe is $1,191m (previously $1,216m) versus consensus of $1,211m.
GSe 2027 EBITDA is $1,315m (unchanged) versus consensus of $1,324m. GS is below consensus in the near term and above it on average from 2028.
GS 4Q26 EBITDA estimate is about $323m, up 11% QoQ. Management guided to high-single-digit sequential growth.
GS EPS estimates are $1.62 for 2026E (previously $1.09), $1.30 for 2027E and $1.48 for 2028E (previously $1.52). The 2026E figure includes the Veolia proceeds.
Adj. FCF after dividends guidance was raised to $700-760m from $330-390m on $377m of Veolia litigation proceeds. GSe is $702m.
risk_factors: Higher capex could reduce capital return opportunities.
Sponsor ownership concentration and corporate governance.
Curtailments by AR that depend on gas prices and season, with weak in-basin pricing and third-party outages cutting AM volumes.
Execution risk on regional pipelines (ESE and North-South), which are pre-FID or in scoping.
Gas prices relative to the levels needed to sustain AR's 2027+ growth plans.

tension_points.bull_case: Management sizes the regional infrastructure opportunity at several billion dollars, driven by demand pull from LNG, utilities and electrification. GS models about $700-800m across ESE and North-South and expects a roughly 7% 2026-2030 EBITDA CAGR.
tension_points.bear_case: A 2027 capex step-up of $100m+ slows buybacks. Curtailments tied to gas prices cut volumes in the near term, and North-South is still pre-FID.
tension_points.what_invalidates: North-South failing to reach FID in 2027, or gas prices falling below the levels needed to support AR's 2027+ growth plans.

theme_stances.key_argument: Demand pull from LNG, utilities and electrification makes regional pipelines a credible growth leg for AM.
